mainTopic: Good wives and bad wives, the "vile nation" and the חברים, sayings of בן סירא, and the great importance of פריה ורביה
overview: The amud opens with the end of a statement that wives save us from sin. רב יהודה calls his own wife both "more bitter than death" and a source of peace of mind. The גמרא explains that she was quick to anger but also quick to calm down. אביי and רבא describe a bad wife, and רבא teaches that it is a מצוה to divorce one, and that if her כתובה is too large to pay, the husband may take a second wife. Several אמוראים read harsh פסוקים as hints to a bad wife with a large כתובה, and others explain the "vile nation" as מינים, naked nations, or the חברים, Persian priests whose three decrees matched three sins of the Jews. After quotes from בן סירא about wives, temptation and life advice, the גמרא turns to פריה ורביה. רבי אסי says משיח comes only when all souls are born. A ברייתא compares not having children to spilling blood and lessening God's image. בן עזאי explains why he himself never married. A new ברייתא begins with a פסוק from במדבר, and its lesson continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Finishing the previous statement: wives save us from sin
steps.stepSummary: These are the closing words of a statement that started before this section. The full point is that wives deserve our thanks, partly because they protect us from sin.
steps.simpleTranslation: …from sin.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a sentence that began earlier. Its point is that a wife protects her husband from sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier statement gives reasons to be grateful to one's wife even when she is difficult. One reason is that marriage keeps a man away from sin. This sets the theme for what follows: good wives and difficult wives.

phrases.english: from sin.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִן הַחֵטְא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a statement that began before this section.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A wife deserves appreciation because, among other things, she protects her husband from sin.

steps.title: רב יהודה points to his own wife as the bitter woman
steps.stepSummary: While teaching his son the פסוק "I find more bitter than death the woman," רב יהודה is asked for an example. He answers: "Your mother."
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה was teaching his son רב יצחק the פסוק "And I find more bitter than death the woman." His son asked, "For example, who?" He answered, "For example, your mother."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a short story. רב יהודה gives his own wife as an example of the "bitter woman" in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק talks about a woman who is worse than death. רב יהודה makes it personal by naming his own wife. This will be a problem in the next step, because elsewhere he praises the same woman.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda was teaching
to Rav Yitzchak, his son,
"And I find more bitter than death the woman."
phrases.notes: קהלת 7:26

phrases.english: He said to him: For example, who?
phrases.notes: The son is the one asking.

phrases.english: For example, your mother.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַקְרֵי לֵיהּ רַב יְהוּדָה לְרַב יִצְחָק בְּרֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of difficult wives with a story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב יהודה described his own wife as an example of the woman "more bitter than death."

steps.title: But רב יהודה also used her as the example of a wife who brings peace
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the story. רב יהודה once taught that a man finds peace of mind only with his first wife, and he gave the same example then: "Your mother."
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רב יהודה teach his son רב יצחק: "A man finds peace of mind only with his first wife, as it says: 'Let your fountain be blessed, and rejoice in the wife of your youth'"? And his son asked, "For example, who?" and he answered, "For example, your mother!"
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a contradiction. רב יהודה called the same woman both bitter and the source of his peace of mind.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 2 his wife is the "bitter woman." Here she is the example of a first wife who brings a man peace. She cannot seem to be both, so the גמרא asks how to reconcile the two statements.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it so that… (opens a challenge)
Was teaching (a teaching or a ברייתא)

phrases.english: But didn't Rav Yehuda teach
to Rav Yitzchak, his son:
A man does not find peace of mind
except with his first wife,
as it says: "Let your fountain be blessed,
and rejoice in the wife of your youth,"
phrases.notes: משלי 5:18

phrases.english: and he said to him: For example, who?
For example, your mother!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא מַתְנֵי לֵיהּ רַב יְהוּדָה לְרַב יִצְחָק בְּרֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the story in step 2 by citing a different teaching from רב יהודה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה's description of his wife as the "bitter woman" (step 2).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: He gave the same wife as the example of a first wife who brings peace of mind, which seems to contradict calling her bitter.

steps.title: She was hot-tempered but calmed down quickly
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that both descriptions are true. She got angry easily, which made her "bitter," but she was easily calmed, which brought him peace.
steps.simpleTranslation: She would flare up in anger, but she was easily won over with a word.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the contradiction. רב יהודה's wife had both sides to her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her quick temper explains why he named her for the "bitter" פסוק. Her quickness to make peace explains why he also named her for the "peace of mind" teaching. The two statements describe different sides of the same person.

keyTerms.meaning: She would get angry and harsh
She was easily calmed with a word

phrases.english: She would flare up,
but she was easily won over with a word.
phrases.notes: Literally, "she lets it pass with a word," meaning one kind word calmed her down.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִתְקָיף תְּקִיפָא וְעַבּוֹרֵי מְיעַבְּרָא בְּמִלַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Both statements are true about different sides of her personality.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two statements contradict each other: she is either bitter or a source of peace.
steps.terutzMaskana: She was quick to anger, so she was "bitter," and quick to forgive, so she brought peace.
steps.whatToRemember: רב יהודה's wife fit both descriptions: she got angry quickly and calmed down quickly.

steps.title: What counts as a bad wife?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for a definition of an אשה רעה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is a bad wife like?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a new question, which sets up the answers of אביי and רבא in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Having talked about a "bitter" wife, the גמרא now wants a concrete picture of what makes a wife truly bad.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it like? What are the circumstances?

phrases.english: What is a bad wife like?

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכִי דָּמֵי אִשָּׁה רָעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the story to a general definition.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The defining features of an אשה רעה.

steps.title: אביי: she sets the table and sets her mouth too
steps.stepSummary: אביי says a bad wife prepares her husband's food but insults him while he eats.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: She sets the table for him, and she sets her mouth for him too.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives his definition of a bad wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: She does her household tasks, but she spoils the meal with harsh words. The problem is her speech, not her work.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
She sets the table for him
and sets her mouth for him.
phrases.notes: She serves the food and scolds him at the same time.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי מְקַשְּׁטָא לֵיהּ תַּכָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A bad wife serves the meal but insults her husband while he eats.

steps.title: רבא: she sets the table and turns her back
steps.stepSummary: רבא says a bad wife prepares the food and then turns her back on her husband.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: She sets the table for him, and then turns her back to him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a different definition of a bad wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבא, the problem is coldness, not insults. She serves the food but shows she has no interest in being with him.

phrases.english: Rava said:
She sets the table for him
and turns her back to him.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר מְקַשְּׁטָא לֵיהּ תַּכָּא וּמַהְדְּרָא לֵיהּ גַּבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to the question in step 5, different from אביי's.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A bad wife serves the meal and then coldly turns away from her husband.
steps.whatToRemember: אביי says a bad wife is harsh with her words; רבא says she is cold and distant.

steps.title: Marriage makes a man's sins crumble away
steps.stepSummary: רבי חמא בר חנינא says that once a man marries, his sins are broken apart. He learns this from the word "ויפק" in a פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חמא בר חנינא said: Once a man marries a woman, his sins crumble away, as it says: "Whoever finds a wife finds good, and obtains favor from 'ה."
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching praises marriage: it brings forgiveness of sins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word "ויפק" (obtains) sounds like "מתפקקין" (crumble). From this sound-alike he learns that marriage breaks apart a man's sins and brings him favor from 'ה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chama bar Chanina said:
Once a man marries a woman,
his sins crumble away,
as it says: "Whoever finds a wife finds good,
and obtains favor from the Lord."
phrases.notes: משלי 18:22. The word ויפק sounds like מתפקקין, and that is the hint.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חָמָא בַּר חֲנִינָא כֵּיוָן שֶׁנָּשָׂא אָדָם אִשָּׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to praising marriage after the discussion of bad wives.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Marriage brings forgiveness of a man's sins, learned from ויפק in משלי.

steps.title: The custom in ארץ ישראל: "מצא" or "מוצא"?
steps.stepSummary: In ארץ ישראל, people would ask a new groom "מצא or מוצא?" They were asking which פסוק fit his wife: the one about finding good, or the one about finding something more bitter than death.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the West, when a man married a woman, they would say to him: "מצא or מוצא?" "מצא," as it is written: "Whoever finds a wife finds good." "מוצא," as it is written: "And I find more bitter than death the woman."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports a custom of asking a groom whether his wife is the good kind or the bitter kind.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two פסוקים about finding a wife begin with almost the same word. "מצא" opens the praise in משלי, and "מוצא" opens the warning in קהלת. The one-word question brings together both sides of the whole discussion: a wife can be a great blessing or very bitter.

keyTerms.meaning: In the West, meaning ארץ ישראל

phrases.english: In the West, when a man married a woman,
phrases.notes: "The West" means ארץ ישראל, which lies west of בבל.

phrases.english: they would say to him like this:
"Matza" or "motze"?
"Matza," as it is written: "Whoever finds a wife finds good,"
"Motze," as it is written:
"And I find more bitter than death the woman."

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּמַעְרְבָא כִּי נָסֵיב אִינָשׁ אִיתְּתָא אָמְרִי לֵיהּ הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the פסוק "מצא אשה" from step 8 and sets it against the קהלת פסוק from step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In ארץ ישראל, a groom was asked which פסוק described his wife: "מצא" (good) or "מוצא" (bitter).
steps.whatToRemember: "מצא" points to the good wife of משלי, and "מוצא" points to the bitter woman of קהלת. The question captures both sides of the whole discussion.
steps.confusionAlert: The two words look almost the same, but they point to opposite פסוקים: מצא is praise, and מוצא is a warning.

steps.title: It is a מצוה to divorce a bad wife
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that there is a מצוה to divorce an אשה רעה, and brings a פסוק from משלי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: It is a מצוה to divorce a bad wife, as it says: 'Cast out the scorner, and fighting will leave; strife and shame will stop.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא moves from describing a bad wife to telling us what to do about her: divorcing her is a מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 6 and 7 described what an אשה רעה is. Now רבא adds a practical rule. He reads the 'scorner' in the פסוק as the bad wife, and says that sending her away brings peace to the home.

keyTerms.meaning: A מצוה, a good deed we are told to do

phrases.english: Rava said:
A bad wife, it is a מצוה to divorce her,
as it is written: "Cast out the scorner and fighting will leave,
phrases.notes: משלי 22:10

phrases.english: and strife and shame will stop."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: אִשָּׁה רָעָה מִצְוָה לְגָרְשָׁהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from defining an אשה רעה to giving a practical rule about her.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is a מצוה to divorce an אשה רעה.

steps.title: When her marriage contract is too large, take a second wife
steps.stepSummary: רבא says that if a bad wife's כתובה is too large to pay, the answer is to marry another wife next to her. He backs this up with a common saying.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא said: A bad wife whose כתובה is large: her rival wife at her side. As people say: you trouble a woman with her rival, not with a thorn.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא covers a case where divorce is too expensive. If the husband can't afford to pay the כתובה, he can marry a second wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 10 said to divorce a bad wife. But divorce means paying the כתובה, and sometimes it is too big. In that case רבא suggests a rival wife, and a folk saying shows that this is what really bothers a woman.

keyTerms.meaning: The marriage contract, which promises the wife money if she is divorced
A rival wife, another wife of the same husband

phrases.english: And Rava said:
A bad wife whose kesubah is large
— her rival wife at her side.
phrases.notes: He can't afford to divorce her, so he should marry a second wife alongside her.

phrases.english: As people say:
With her fellow wife, and not with a thorn.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רָבָא: אִשָּׁה רָעָה וּכְתוּבָּתָהּ מְרוּבָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Covers the case where the divorce from step 10 is too costly.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If her כתובה is too large to pay, the husband may take another wife next to her.

steps.title: A bad wife is like a day of steady rain
steps.stepSummary: רבא compares a bad wife to a dreary, rainy day, based on a פסוק in משלי.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא said: A bad wife is as hard as a day of heavy rain, as it says: 'A constant drip on a rainy day and a quarrelsome woman are alike.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a picture to show how hard it is to live with a bad wife: it feels like rain that never stops dripping.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This adds no new rule. It describes the feeling. The פסוק compares the quarrelsome woman to a leaking roof on a rainy day, which wears a person down without stopping.

keyTerms.meaning: A day of heavy, steady rain

phrases.english: And Rava said:
A bad wife is as hard as a day of heavy rain,
as it is said: "A constant drip on a rainy day
phrases.notes: משלי 27:15

phrases.english: and a quarrelsome woman are alike."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רָבָא: קָשָׁה אִשָּׁה רָעָה כְּיוֹם סַגְרִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another teaching of רבא in the same series about an אשה רעה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A bad wife is as hard to bear as a day of steady rain.

steps.title: How good a good wife is, whichever way the verse is read
steps.stepSummary: רבא opens a two-part teaching. First he shows from 'מצא אשה מצא טוב' that a good wife is very good, whether the פסוק is about a real wife or about the תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא said: Come and see how good a good wife is and how bad a bad wife is. How good is a good wife? As it says: 'Whoever finds a wife finds good.' If the verse is about a wife, she is very good, since the verse praises her. If the verse is about the תורה, she is still very good, since the תורה is compared to her.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא states both sides, good and bad, and starts with the good side. Whichever way you read the פסוק, a good wife comes out praised.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some read 'wife' in this פסוק as a picture for the תורה. רבא says it doesn't matter. If it is about a real wife, the פסוק praises her. If it is about the תורה, then the תורה is being compared to a good wife, which shows how highly she is valued. This is the same פסוק the people of ארץ ישראל asked new grooms about in step 9.

phrases.english: And Rava said: Come and see
how good a good wife is,
and how bad a bad wife is.
How good is a good wife?
As it is written: "Whoever finds a wife finds good."
phrases.notes: משלי 18:22

phrases.english: If the verse is talking about her, a real wife,

phrases.aramaic: — כַּמָּה טוֹבָה אִשָּׁה טוֹבָה, שֶׁהַכָּתוּב מְשַׁבְּחָהּ.
phrases.english: — how good a good wife is, since the verse praises her.
If the verse is talking about the Torah,

phrases.aramaic: — כַּמָּה טוֹבָה אִשָּׁה טוֹבָה, שֶׁהַתּוֹרָה נִמְשְׁלָה בָּהּ.
phrases.english: — how good a good wife is, since the Torah is compared to her.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רָבָא: בֹּא וּרְאֵה כַּמָּה טוֹבָה אִשָּׁה טוֹבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the 'מצא' פסוק from step 9 and shows its praise holds however it is read.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A good wife is very good, whether the פסוק is about a wife or about the תורה.

steps.title: How bad a bad wife is, whichever way the verse is read
steps.stepSummary: רבא finishes his teaching. From 'מוצא אני מר ממות' he shows that a bad wife is very bad, whether the פסוק is about a real woman or about גיהנם.
steps.simpleTranslation: How bad is a bad wife? As it says: 'I find more bitter than death the woman.' If the verse is about her, she is very bad, since the verse condemns her. If it is about גיהנם, she is still very bad, since גיהנם is compared to her.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the second half of רבא's teaching from step 13. Now he shows the bad side with the 'מוצא' פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It follows the same pattern as step 13. If the פסוק is about a real woman, it puts her down. If 'the woman' is a picture for גיהנם, then גיהנם is compared to a bad wife, which shows how terrible she is.

keyTerms.meaning: גיהנם, the place of punishment after death

steps.whatToRemember: רבא's pattern: whether the פסוק is about a real wife or is a picture (for תורה or for גיהנם), a good wife comes out very good and a bad wife comes out very bad.

phrases.english: How bad is a bad wife?

phrases.aramaic: דִּכְתִיב: ״וּמוֹצֶא אֲנִי מַר מִמָּוֶת אֶת הָאִשָּׁה״.
phrases.english: As it is written: "And I find more bitter than death the woman."
phrases.notes: קהלת 7:26

phrases.english: If the verse is talking about her,

phrases.aramaic: — כַּמָּה רָעָה אִשָּׁה רָעָה, שֶׁהַכָּתוּב מְגַנֶּהָ.
phrases.english: — how bad a bad wife is, since the verse condemns her.
If the verse is talking about Gehinnom,

phrases.aramaic: — כַּמָּה רָעָה אִשָּׁה רָעָה, שֶׁגֵּיהִנָּם נִמְשְׁלָה בָּהּ.
phrases.english: — how bad a bad wife is, since Gehinnom is compared to her.

steps.triggerLanguage: כַּמָּה רָעָה אִשָּׁה רָעָה, דִּכְתִיב: ״וּמוֹצֶא אֲנִי מַר מִמָּוֶת אֶת הָאִשָּׁה״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the second half of the teaching opened in step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A bad wife is very bad, whether the פסוק is about a woman or about גיהנם.

steps.title: An evil they cannot escape is a bad wife with a large כתובה
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן, quoting רבה בר אבוה, reads a פסוק in ירמיהו about an inescapable evil as referring to a bad wife whose כתובה is large.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Behold, I am bringing evil that they will not be able to escape.' רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה: This is a bad wife whose כתובה is large.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new set of teachings in which harsh פסוקים are read as hints to a bad wife with a large כתובה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This connects back to step 11. A bad wife with a big כתובה is an evil you 'cannot escape', because divorcing her costs too much. That fits the פסוק's wording well.

keyTerms.meaning: To get out of it, to escape it

phrases.english: "Behold, I am bringing evil
phrases.notes: ירמיהו 11:11

phrases.english: that they will not be able to escape."

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ:
phrases.english: Rav Nachman said in the name of Rabba bar Avuh:
This is a bad wife whose kesubah is large.

steps.triggerLanguage: ״הִנְנִי מֵבִיא רָעָה אֲשֶׁר לֹא יוּכְלוּ לָצֵאת מִמֶּנָּה״, אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a series of פסוקים read as hints to the case from step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The inescapable evil in ירמיהו is a bad wife with a large כתובה.

steps.title: Given into hands I cannot rise from
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא, quoting מר עוקבא בר חייא, reads a פסוק in איכה the same way: it is about a bad wife with a large כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'ה׳ has given me into the hands of those I cannot stand up against.' רב חסדא said in the name of מר עוקבא בר חייא: This is a bad wife whose כתובה is large.
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא reads another פסוק, this one from איכה, as describing the same trapped husband.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is the same as step 15: the husband is stuck and 'cannot get up' and leave, because the כתובה is too big to pay.

keyTerms.meaning: I cannot get up, I cannot stand

phrases.english: "ה׳ has given me into the hands of those I cannot stand up against."
phrases.notes: איכה 1:14

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר מָר עוּקְבָא בַּר חִיָּיא:
phrases.english: Rav Chisda said in the name of Mar Ukva bar Chiya:
This is a bad wife whose kesubah is large.

steps.triggerLanguage: ״נְתָנַנִי ה׳ בִּידֵי לֹא אוּכַל קוּם״, אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר מָר עוּקְבָא בַּר חִיָּיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second פסוק given the same reading as step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פסוק in איכה is about a bad wife with a large כתובה.

steps.title: In the West: one who must buy all his food
steps.stepSummary: In ארץ ישראל they read the פסוק in איכה differently: it is about a man who has to buy all his food with cash.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the West they said: This is one whose food depends on his money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different reading of the same פסוק from איכה, from the חכמים of ארץ ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of a bad wife, they say the man who 'cannot get up' is one who owns no field, so he must pay for every meal. He is always under pressure and never free of worry.

keyTerms.meaning: Food, what a person lives on

phrases.english: In the West they said:
phrases.notes: 'The West' means ארץ ישראל.

phrases.english: This is one whose food depends on his money.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּמַעְרְבָא אָמְרוּ: זֶה שֶׁמְּזוֹנוֹתָיו תְּלוּיִן בְּכַסְפּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different reading of the same פסוק discussed in step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פסוק in איכה is about a man who must buy all his food.

steps.title: Children given to another people is a stepmother
steps.stepSummary: רב חנן בר רבא, quoting רב, reads a curse from the תורה about children being 'given to another people' as being about a stepmother.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Your sons and daughters will be given to another people.' רב חנן בר רבא said in the name of רב: This is the father's wife.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another פסוק read as a hint to home life. This time the 'other people' is a stepmother raising the children.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Children raised by a stepmother can feel like strangers handed to 'another people.' This reading sets up the next step, where the same רב reads a nearby פסוק as being about a bad wife.

phrases.english: "Your sons and your daughters will be given to another people."
phrases.notes: דברים 28:32

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חָנָן בַּר רָבָא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rav Chanan bar Rava said in the name of Rav:
This is the father's wife.

steps.triggerLanguage: ״בָּנֶיךָ וּבְנוֹתֶיךָ נְתוּנִים לְעַם אַחֵר״, אָמַר רַב חָנָן בַּר רָבָא אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another פסוק read as a hint to troubles at home.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'Given to another people' is about a stepmother.

steps.title: A vile nation is a bad wife with a large כתובה
steps.stepSummary: The same רב חנן בר רבא, quoting רב, reads 'I will anger them with a vile nation' as being about a bad wife with a large כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'I will anger them with a vile nation.' רב חנן בר רבא said in the name of רב: This is a bad wife whose כתובה is large.
steps.whatsHappening: רב reads another פסוק from the תורה as describing the trapped husband of a bad wife with a big כתובה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The punishment here is being made angry, and this wife is a constant source of anger the husband can't get rid of. The next step brings a different view of who the 'vile nation' is.

phrases.english: "With a vile nation I will anger them."
phrases.notes: דברים 32:21

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חָנָן בַּר רָבָא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rav Chanan bar Rava said in the name of Rav:
This is a bad wife whose kesubah is large.

steps.triggerLanguage: ״בְּגוֹי נָבָל אַכְעִיסֵם״, אָמַר רַב חָנָן בַּר רָבָא אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same speaker as step 18, now reading a פסוק the same way as steps 15 and 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The 'vile nation' is a bad wife with a large כתובה.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: the vile nation is heretics
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר disagrees and says the 'vile nation' is the מינים. He proves it from a פסוק in תהלים that calls a person who denies ה׳ a 'נבל'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: These are the heretics. And so it says: 'The vile man said in his heart, There is no God.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר gives a different reading of the 'vile nation' from step 19 and backs it up with a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He links the two פסוקים through the word 'נבל.' In תהלים, the 'נבל' is the one who says there is no God. So the 'vile nation' in דברים must also be people who deny ה׳, the מינים.

keyTerms.meaning: Heretics, people who deny the תורה
And so it says (brings a supporting פסוק)

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says: These are the heretics.
And so it says:
"The vile man said in his heart: There is no God, etc."
phrases.notes: תהלים 14:1. The word נבל here links back to the 'vile nation' in the previous פסוק.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: אֵלּוּ הַמִּינִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different reading of the פסוק from step 19.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The 'vile nation' refers to מינים, as shown by the use of 'נבל' in תהלים.
steps.whatToRemember: Many פסוקים about suffering are read as hinting to a bad wife with a large כתובה, a trap the husband can't escape. Others read some of these פסוקים differently: as a man who must buy all his food, or as מינים.

steps.title: A ברייתא: the vile nation are people who walk naked in public
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says the 'vile nation' are the people of Barbarya and Martenai, who walk naked in the marketplace, which ה׳ finds disgusting.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא taught: These are the people of Barbarya and the people of Martenai, who walk around naked in the marketplace. Nothing is more despised and disgusting before ה׳ than someone who walks naked in the marketplace.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third explanation of 'I will anger them with a vile nation.' This one comes from a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 19 said the 'vile nation' is a bad wife, and step 20 said it is the מינים. This ברייתא says it is a real nation whose people walk naked in public. It explains why they are called 'vile': public nakedness is extremely disgusting to ה׳.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא (a teaching from the time of the משנה that is not in the משנה itself)
Literally 'the Place'; a name for ה׳

phrases.english: It was taught in a ברייתא:
phrases.notes: This is still explaining 'I will anger them with a vile nation' from step 19.

phrases.english: These are the people of Barbarya
and the people of Martenai,
who walk naked in the marketplace.
For there is nobody more despised and disgusting
before ה׳
than someone who walks naked in the marketplace.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּמַתְנִיתָא תָּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives another explanation of the same פסוק discussed in steps 19 and 20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The 'vile nation' are the people of Barbarya and Martenai, who walk naked in public.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: the vile nation are the חברים
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says the 'vile nation' are the חברים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: These are the חברים.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives yet another explanation of the 'vile nation.' He says it refers to the חברים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a fourth view of the same פסוק. Here the חברים are a group of Persian priests who made life hard for the Jews. They are not 'friends' or Torah scholars, even though the word looks the same.

keyTerms.meaning: Here, a group of harsh Persian priests (not 'friends')

steps.confusionAlert: In this sugya, חברים does NOT mean friends or Torah scholars. It is the name of a group of Persian priests who oppressed the Jews.

phrases.english: רבי יוחנן said:
These are the חברים.
phrases.notes: Here this is a group of Persian priests, not 'friends.'

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the ברייתא in step 21 about who the 'vile nation' is.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The 'vile nation' are the חברים.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן falls in fear, then sits up when he hears they take bribes
steps.stepSummary: When told the חברים came to בבל, רבי יוחנן shook and fell. When told they accept bribes, he straightened up and sat down again.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to רבי יוחנן: The חברים have come to בבל. He shook and fell. They said to him: They accept bribes. He straightened up and sat down.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a short story about רבי יוחנן and the חברים. It shows how dangerous they were, and that there was still a way to deal with them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן was so afraid for the Jews of בבל that he fell. Once he heard the חברים could be paid off, he knew the Jews could protect themselves, so he calmed down. The story supports calling the חברים a 'vile nation.'

phrases.english: They said to רבי יוחנן:
The חברים have come to בבל,
he shook and fell.
phrases.notes: He was scared for the Jews living in בבל.

phrases.english: They said to him:
They accept bribes,
he straightened up and sat down.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A story about the חברים that רבי יוחנן just mentioned.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The חברים were very dangerous, but they could be bribed.

steps.title: Three decrees of the חברים: meat and bathhouses
steps.stepSummary: The חברים made three decrees because of three sins. They banned meat because the Jews did not give the מתנות, and bathhouses because the Jews neglected טבילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: They made decrees about three things because of three sins. They decreed against meat because of the gifts. They decreed against the bathhouses because of immersion.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the חברים were just mentioned, the גמרא brings a teaching about three decrees they made against the Jews. It gives the first two here, and the third comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each decree matches the sin that caused it. The Jews did not give the כהן his מתנות from their meat, so they lost their meat. They did not go to the מקוה for טבילה, so they lost their bathhouses.

keyTerms.meaning: The gifts from an animal that are given to a כהן

phrases.english: They made decrees about three things
phrases.notes: 'They' are the חברים from the last step.

phrases.english: because of three sins.
They decreed against meat —
because of the gifts,
phrases.notes: The Jews were not giving the כהן his parts of the animal.

phrases.english: they decreed against the bathhouses —
because of immersion.

steps.triggerLanguage: גָּזְרוּ עַל שְׁלֹשָׁה מִפְּנֵי שְׁלֹשָׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from who the חברים were to what they did to the Jews.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The חברים' decrees against meat and bathhouses came because the Jews neglected the מתנות and טבילה.

steps.title: The third decree: digging up the dead
steps.stepSummary: The third decree was digging up the dead, because the Jews rejoiced on the non-Jews' holidays. The source is a פסוק that mentions 'you and your fathers.'
steps.simpleTranslation: They dig up the dead, because the Jews rejoice on the non-Jews' holidays. As it says: 'Then the hand of ה׳ will be against you and against your fathers.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the third decree of the חברים and brings a פסוק as its source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sin was joining in the non-Jews' holidays, and the punishment was having their dead dug up. The פסוק says ה׳'s hand will be 'against your fathers,' meaning even those already dead. The next step explains how the פסוק fits.

phrases.english: They dig up the dead —
because the Jews rejoice on their holidays.
phrases.notes: 'Their' means the non-Jews' holidays.

phrases.english: As it is said:
'Then the hand of ה׳ will be against you and against your fathers.'
phrases.notes: שמואל א 12:15

steps.triggerLanguage: קָא מְחַטְּטִי שָׁכְבֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the list of three decrees started in step 24.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The חברים dug up Jewish graves because the Jews joined in non-Jewish holidays.

steps.title: רבה בר שמואל: the פסוק means digging up the dead
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר שמואל explains that the פסוק about 'your fathers' means digging up the dead, because the living's sins cause the dead to be dug up.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר שמואל said: This means digging up the dead. As the Master said: Because of the sins of the living, the dead are dug up.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר שמואל explains how the פסוק from the last step connects to digging up the dead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: How can ה׳'s hand be 'against your fathers' who already died? רבה בר שמואל answers: their graves are dug up. He backs this up with a known saying that the sins of the living cause the dead to be dug up.

keyTerms.meaning: As the Master said (quoting a known teaching)
Because of the sin of the living

phrases.english: רבה בר שמואל said:
This is the digging up of the dead.
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the word in round brackets; the meaning stays the same.

phrases.english: As the Master said:
Because of the sin of the living —
the dead are dug up.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the פסוק in step 25 fits the third decree.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'Against your fathers' refers to the dead being dug up because of the sins of the living.

steps.title: רבא asks: how can death be chosen if the dead lie unburied?
steps.stepSummary: רבא points out that one פסוק says the dead will lie unburied like dung, but the next פסוק says death will be chosen over life.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to רבה בר מארי: It is written, 'They will not be gathered and not be buried; they will be like dung on the ground.' And it is written, 'And death will be chosen over life.'
steps.whatsHappening: Still on the topic of disturbing the dead, רבא asks about two פסוקים in ירמיהו that seem to contradict each other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first פסוק describes a terrible death, with bodies left unburied. So how can the very next פסוק say people will prefer death to life? Who would want such a death?

keyTerms.meaning: And death will be chosen over life

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא לְרַבָּה בַּר מָארִי,
phrases.english: רבא said to רבה בר מארי:
It is written: 'They will not be gathered and will not be buried;
they will be like dung on the face of the ground,'
phrases.notes: ירמיהו 8:2

phrases.english: and it is written: 'And death will be chosen over life.'
phrases.notes: ירמיהו 8:3, the very next פסוק.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא לְרַבָּה בַּר מָארִי כְּתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of the dead being disturbed, now with a question on פסוקים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If death means lying unburied like dung, it makes no sense that people would choose death over life.

steps.title: רבה בר מארי: death is better for the wicked so they stop sinning
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר מארי answers that death is better for the wicked, so they will not keep living, sinning, and falling into גיהנם.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Death is chosen for the wicked, so that they will not live in this world and sin, and fall into גיהנם.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר מארי answers רבא's question by explaining what 'death will be chosen' really means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The second פסוק is not saying the unburied death is pleasant. It means that for wicked people it is better to die than to keep living and adding sins. More years of sinning would only bring them deeper into גיהנם.

keyTerms.meaning: גיהנם, the place of punishment after death

steps.whatToRemember: The 'vile nation' has many explanations (a bad wife, מינים, naked nations, the חברים). The חברים' three decrees each matched a Jewish sin. And for the wicked, death can be 'chosen' because it stops them from sinning more.

phrases.english: He said to him:
Death is chosen for the wicked,
so that they will not live in this world and sin,
and fall into גיהנם.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ נִבְחַר מָוֶת לָרְשָׁעִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's question from step 27.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Death will be chosen' seemed to mean the unburied death itself was preferable to life.
steps.terutzMaskana: Death is better for the wicked only because it stops them from sinning more and sinking deeper into גיהנם.

steps.title: בן סירא on good, bad, and beautiful wives
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes ספר בן סירא. A good wife is a gift, a bad wife is like צרעת whose cure is divorce, and a beautiful wife doubles her husband's days.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is written in the book of בן סירא: "A good wife is a good gift for her husband," and it says: "A good one will be given to a God-fearing man." "A bad wife is a plague to her husband." What is his fix? "He should divorce her and be healed of his plague." "A beautiful wife: happy is her husband, his days are doubled."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to its topic of wives. It quotes sayings from ספר בן סירא about what a good wife, a bad wife, and a beautiful wife mean for a husband.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are three kinds of wife here. A good one is a gift, and she is given to someone who fears God. A bad one is like צרעת, and divorce is presented as the cure. A beautiful one makes her husband so happy that it feels like he lives twice as long.

keyTerms.meaning: The book of בן סירא, a collection of wise sayings that the גמרא quotes here
A plague-like skin disease, used here as a picture of a terrible burden

phrases.english: It is written in the book of Ben Sira:
"A good wife is a good gift for her husband,"
and it is written: "A good one will be placed in the bosom of a God-fearing man."
phrases.notes: This is still quoting from בן סירא, not a new source.

phrases.english: "A bad wife is a plague to her husband."
What is his remedy?
"He should divorce her and be cured of his plague."
"A beautiful wife: happy is her husband;
the number of his days is doubled."

steps.triggerLanguage: כָּתוּב בְּסֵפֶר בֶּן סִירָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side-topic of the חברים and returns to the larger theme of wives.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A good wife is a gift, a bad wife is a plague that divorce can cure, and a beautiful wife doubles her husband's days.

steps.title: Warning to stay away from another man's attractive wife
steps.stepSummary: בן סירא warns not to look at a married woman's charm or drink with her husband to get close to her. Many have been ruined this way, and getting used to such things spreads like fire.
steps.simpleTranslation: "Turn your eyes away from a charming woman, or you will be caught in her trap. Do not go over to her husband to drink wine and strong drink with him, because many have been ruined by a beautiful woman's looks, and her victims are many and mighty." "Many were the wounds of the peddler." "People who get used to forbidden relations are like a spark that lights a coal. Like a cage full of birds, their houses are full of deceit."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps quoting בן סירא. Now it moves from a man's own wife to a warning about getting close to someone else's wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The danger builds step by step. It starts with looking, then with getting friendly with the husband as an excuse to be near her. The spark-and-coal picture teaches that a small habit can grow into a big fire of sin. The cage picture shows that such homes fill up with lies.

phrases.english: "Turn your eyes away from a graceful woman
lest you be caught in her trap.
Do not turn aside to her husband
to mix wine and strong drink with him,

phrases.aramaic: כִּי בְּתוֹאַר אִשָּׁה יָפָה רַבִּים הוּשְׁחֲתוּ,
phrases.english: for through the looks of a beautiful woman many have been destroyed,
and mighty are all her slain."
"Many were the wounds of the peddler."
phrases.notes: Peddlers sold jewelry to women and spent a lot of time with them, and they got hurt for it.

phrases.english: "Those who accustom themselves to forbidden relations
are like a spark that ignites a coal.
Like a cage full of birds,
so are their houses full of deceit."

steps.triggerLanguage: הַעְלֵם עֵינֶיךָ מֵאֵשֶׁת חֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues quoting בן סירא, moving from one's own wife to the danger of another man's wife.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Keep away from another man's attractive wife, because small steps toward sin grow into great destruction.

steps.title: בן סירא's advice on worry, guests, and secrets
steps.stepSummary: More sayings from בן סירא. Don't worry about tomorrow, since you may not be alive for it. Don't let crowds into your house. Have many well-wishers, but share secrets with very few.
steps.simpleTranslation: "Don't worry about tomorrow's trouble, because you don't know what a day will bring. Maybe tomorrow comes and he is gone, and it turns out he worried about a world that isn't his." "Keep crowds out of your house, and don't bring everyone in." "Let many people care about your welfare, but tell a secret to only one in a thousand."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its list of בן סירא quotes with general life advice that is not about wives.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first saying teaches that worrying about the future is wasted, since a person may not live to see it. The next sayings balance two things. Be friendly with many people, but keep your home private and trust very few with secrets.

keyTerms.meaning: People who ask about your well-being, your friends

steps.whatToRemember: The בן סירא section ends here. It covered good and bad wives, staying away from another man's wife, and general advice about worry, guests, and secrets.

phrases.english: "Do not suffer over tomorrow's trouble,

phrases.aramaic: כִּי לֹא תֵדַע מַה יֵּלֶד יוֹם.
phrases.english: for you do not know what a day will bring.
Perhaps tomorrow comes and he is no more,

phrases.aramaic: נִמְצָא מִצְטַעֵר עַל הָעוֹלָם שֶׁאֵין שֶׁלּוֹ״.
phrases.english: and it turns out he was upset over a world that is not his."
"Keep the crowd out of your house,
and do not bring everyone into your house."
"Let many be those who seek your welfare,
but reveal a secret to one in a thousand."

steps.triggerLanguage: אַל תֵּצַר צָרַת מָחָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues and closes the list of quotes from בן סירא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Don't worry about the future, keep your home private, and trust very few people with secrets.

steps.title: משיח comes only after all souls are born
steps.stepSummary: רבי אסי says משיח will not come until every soul waiting to enter a body has done so. He learns this from a פסוק in ישעיהו.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אסי said: The son of דוד (משיח) will not come until all the souls in the "body" are used up, as it says: "For the spirit that wraps itself is from Me, and the souls that I have made."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the main theme of the sugya, having children. רבי אסי gives a big reason why having children matters: it brings משיח closer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a set number of souls that must come into the world before משיח arrives. Every child born uses up one of those souls. So having children helps bring the redemption.

keyTerms.meaning: The son of דוד, meaning משיח
Literally "body"; here the place where souls wait before being born

steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why פריה ורביה is not only a personal מצוה. It is tied to the redemption of the whole world.

phrases.english: Rabbi Asi said:
The son of David will not come
until all the souls in the "body" are finished,
phrases.notes: He means every soul waiting to be born has to come into the world first.

phrases.english: as it is said:
"For the spirit that enwraps itself is from Me,
and the souls that I have made."
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 57:16

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the בן סירא quotes and goes back to the theme of having children.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: משיח will not come until every soul destined to be born has entered a body.

steps.title: Not having children is like spilling blood
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא brings רבי אליעזר, who says that a person who does not do פריה ורביה is like a murderer. The proof is that the פסוק about spilling blood is placed right before "be fruitful and multiply."
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: רבי אליעזר says: Anyone who does not engage in having children is as if he spills blood, as it says: "Whoever spills man's blood, by man his blood shall be spilled," and right after that it says: "And you, be fruitful and multiply."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that makes a very strong statement about the מצוה of having children, and it gives a source from the תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר learns from the order of the פסוקים. Because "be fruitful and multiply" comes right after the punishment for murder, the תורה is linking them. Not bringing people into the world is compared to taking people out of it.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא
One who spills blood, a murderer

steps.confusionAlert: רבי אליעזר does not say the person is actually a murderer. He says it is כְּאִילּוּ, "as if" he spilled blood. It is a comparison to show how serious the מצוה is.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two big reasons for פריה ורביה in this section. It brings משיח closer (רבי אסי), and not doing it is compared to spilling blood (רבי אליעזר).

phrases.english: It is taught in a baraita: Rabbi Eliezer says:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל מִי שֶׁאֵין עוֹסֵק בִּפְרִיָּה וּרְבִיָּה —
phrases.english: Anyone who does not engage in being fruitful and multiplying
is as though he sheds blood,
as it is said:
"Whoever sheds the blood of man, by man shall his blood be shed,"
phrases.notes: בראשית 9:6

phrases.english: and it is written right after it:
"And you, be fruitful and multiply."
phrases.notes: בראשית 9:7. Because the two פסוקים sit next to each other, he links them.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second statement about how important having children is, after רבי אסי's statement.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who does not engage in פריה ורביה is considered as if he spilled blood, learned from the closeness of בראשית 9:6 and 9:7.

steps.title: רבי יעקב: Not having children lessens God's image
steps.stepSummary: רבי יעקב says that someone who does not do פריה ורביה is like one who lessens the צלם אלקים. He proves it from the order of the פסוקים in בראשית.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יעקב says: It is as if he makes God's image smaller. The פסוק says, 'For in the image of God He made man,' and right after it is written, 'And you, be fruitful and multiply.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with a second opinion. רבי יעקב gives a different reason why not having children is so serious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר looked at the first half of בראשית ט:ו, 'whoever sheds the blood of man.' רבי יעקב looks at the second half of the same פסוק, 'in the image of God He made man.' Since 'be fruitful' comes right after it, not having children means fewer people carrying God's image in the world.

keyTerms.meaning: lessens the image, meaning there are fewer people in the world who carry God's image
the image of God that man was created in

phrases.english: Rabbi Ya'akov says:
It is as though he diminishes the image,
phrases.notes: He means God's image. Every person born is another 'copy' of that image in the world.

phrases.english: as it is stated: "For in the image of God
He made man"
phrases.notes: בראשית ט:ו

phrases.english: and it is written right after it: "And you, be fruitful, etc."
phrases.notes: בראשית ט:ז

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב אוֹמֵר: כְּאִילּוּ מְמַעֵט הַדְּמוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second view in the same ברייתא, next to רבי אליעזר's 'like a murderer' view.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Not having children is like lessening the צלם אלקים, because 'be fruitful' comes right after the words about the image of God.

steps.title: בן עזאי: It is both shedding blood and lessening the image
steps.stepSummary: בן עזאי combines the two views. Not having children is both like שפיכות דמים and like ממעט הדמות.
steps.simpleTranslation: בן עזאי says: It is as if he both sheds blood and makes God's image smaller, as it says, 'And you, be fruitful and multiply.'
steps.whatsHappening: A third opinion in the ברייתא. בן עזאי says both earlier reasons are true together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק before 'be fruitful' (בראשית ט:ו) mentions both spilling blood and the image of God. רבי אליעזר used one half and רבי יעקב used the other half. בן עזאי uses the whole פסוק, so he says it is both.

keyTerms.meaning: one who spills blood, a murderer
be fruitful and multiply, the מצוה to have children

phrases.english: Ben Azzai says:
It is as though he sheds blood and diminishes the image,
as it is stated: "And you, be fruitful and multiply."
phrases.notes: This פסוק comes right after the one that mentions both spilling blood and God's image, so he takes both.

steps.triggerLanguage: בֶּן עַזַּאי אוֹמֵר: כְּאִילּוּ שׁוֹפֵךְ דָּמִים וּמְמַעֵט הַדְּמוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Joins together the views of רבי אליעזר (Step 33) and רבי יעקב (Step 34).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Not having children is both like שפיכות דמים and like lessening the צלם אלקים.

steps.title: The חכמים challenge בן עזאי for not practicing what he teaches
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים point out that בן עזאי teaches the strongest view about having children, yet he himself never married.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to בן עזאי: Some people teach well and also live up to it. Some live up to it well but don't teach it well. But you teach it well and don't live up to it.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים challenge בן עזאי personally. His teaching does not match how he lives.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not an attack on his דרשה itself. It is a challenge to his conduct. He gave the harshest view of not having children, yet he has no wife and no children.

keyTerms.meaning: lives up to it well, keeps what he teaches

phrases.english: They said to Ben Azzai:
There is one who expounds well and fulfills well,
one who fulfills well but does not expound well,
but you expound well,
and do not fulfill well.
phrases.notes: בן עזאי never got married, so he wasn't doing פריה ורביה himself.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ לְבֶן עַזַּאי: יֵשׁ נָאֶה דּוֹרֵשׁ וְנָאֶה מְקַיֵּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the speaker of Step 35 on his personal conduct.
steps.kashyaTarget: בן עזאי's own behavior compared with his teaching
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If not having children is as bad as murder and lessening God's image, how can he himself stay unmarried?

steps.title: בן עזאי: My soul longs for תורה
steps.stepSummary: בן עזאי answers that his soul is so attached to תורה that he cannot do anything else, and the world can continue through other people.
steps.simpleTranslation: בן עזאי said to them: What can I do? My soul longs for תורה. The world can keep going through other people.
steps.whatsHappening: בן עזאי answers the challenge. He explains why he personally did not marry.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He does not take back his teaching. He agrees having children is vital. He only explains that his own love for תורה is so total that he cannot do it, and the world's need for people can be filled by others.

keyTerms.meaning: my soul longs, is deeply attached

steps.whatToRemember: בן עזאי holds the strongest view of פריה ורביה, yet he explains his own unmarried life as a special case of total love for תורה. He does not change his teaching.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't read this as בן עזאי saying the מצוה doesn't matter. He just explained why it is so serious. He is describing his own unusual situation, not a general permission.

phrases.english: Ben Azzai said to them:
And what shall I do,
since my soul yearns for Torah;
it is possible for the world
to be kept going by others.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶן בֶּן עַזַּאי: וּמָה אֶעֱשֶׂה שֶׁנַּפְשִׁי חָשְׁקָה בַּתּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the personal challenge of Step 36.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Personal exception: the teaching stands, and his own situation is special.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: His not marrying shows he does not really believe what he teaches.
steps.terutzMaskana: He believes it fully, but his soul is bound up with תורה, and others can fill the world.

steps.title: Another version of the same ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: A different ברייתא gives the same discussion. Here רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, not רבי יעקב, holds the 'lessens the image' view. The rest is shortened with 'etc.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Another ברייתא teaches: רבי אליעזר says: Anyone who does not take part in פריה ורביה is like one who spills blood. The פסוק says, 'Whoever sheds the blood of man,' and next to it, 'And you, be fruitful.' רבי אלעזר בן עזריה says: It is as if he lessens the image. בן עזאי says, etc. They said to בן עזאי: There is one who teaches well, etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a second version of the same ברייתא. The main difference is who holds the second opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר's view and proof are the same as in Step 33. The 'image' view is said here in the name of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה instead of רבי יעקב. The parts about בן עזאי are cut short with 'וכו׳' because they match what we already learned.

keyTerms.meaning: it is taught in another ברייתא
etc., the rest is the same as before

phrases.english: It is taught in another ברייתא:
Rabbi Eliezer says:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל מִי שֶׁאֵין עוֹסֵק בִּפְרִיָּה וּרְבִיָּה —
phrases.english: Anyone who does not engage in being fruitful and multiplying
is as though he sheds blood,
as it is stated: "Whoever sheds the blood of man"
phrases.notes: בראשית ט:ו

phrases.english: and next to it: "And you, be fruitful, etc."
Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya says:
It is as though he diminishes the image.
phrases.notes: In this version he is the one saying what רבי יעקב said in Step 34.

phrases.english: Ben Azzai says, etc.

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ לוֹ לְבֶן עַזַּאי: יֵשׁ נָאֶה דּוֹרֵשׁ וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: They said to Ben Azzai: There is one who expounds well, etc.
phrases.notes: The 'etc.' means the whole back-and-forth from Steps 36 and 37 is the same here.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא אִידַּךְ, רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a parallel version of the ברייתא from Steps 33–37, with a different name for the middle opinion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Same three views as before, but the 'lessens the image' view belongs to רבי אלעזר בן עזריה.

steps.title: New ברייתא opens: 'Return, ה׳, to the myriads of thousands of Israel'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a new ברייתא about פריה ורביה by quoting a פסוק from במדבר. The teaching drawn from it continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: 'And when it rested, he would say: Return, ה׳, to the many thousands of Israel.'
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא quotes a פסוק to begin a new teaching, and the explanation comes on the next amud (64a).
steps.deeperAnalysis: So far only the פסוק has been quoted, with no lesson yet. The words 'many thousands of Israel' hint at the number of Jewish people, which ties back to the theme of having children.

keyTerms.meaning: the tens of thousands of thousands of Israel

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
"And when it rested, he would say:
phrases.notes: במדבר י:לו. 'It' is the ארון, and 'he' is משה.

phrases.english: Return, Lord,
to the ten thousands of the thousands of Israel"

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: ״וּבְנֻחֹה יֹאמַר שׁוּבָה ה׳ רִבְבוֹת אַלְפֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new ברייתא on the same general theme of פריה ורביה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only the פסוק is quoted so far. The teaching from it continues on the next amud.
